title: November 18 — WaveFormer: resonant recurrence with attention
summary: WaveFormer now includes a runnable tiny hybrid architecture (ordinary attention, phase-disabled leaky recurrence, resonant recurrent head), a synthetic two-slot memory task and passing CPU unit/smoke tests. Full held-out training and a wave-specific performance advantage are not yet measured. Qwenimagination V2/V3 positive external transfer and V5/V6 negative delayed-write boundaries remain separate.

nodes.claim: Executable tiny two-block causal transformer experiment comparing two attention heads against one attention + leaky recurrent head and one attention + resonant state head, with matching episode streams.
nodes.survived: Source now includes causal attention/RoPE, phase-rotating and phase-disabled heads, balanced two-role generator, training/evaluation runner, five CPU unit tests and a passing two-step CPU smoke run on GitHub Actions (Nov 18). No trained outcome is reported.
nodes.killed: Scientific benchmark still pending. A smoke test is plumbing only; attention versus recurrence accuracy and wave-specific benefit are unknown. No pretrained Qwen integration, long-term native memory or text-generating language model yet.

edges.why: Off-token concept transfer motivates a learned recurrent read/write interface, but there is no shared implementation.
The two-form content/prediction distinction informs a proposed resonant head; waves have not yet earned a numerical advantage.
Distributed persistent context motivates future local gates, not yet implemented in WaveFormer.

motifs.title: Precise attention alongside persistent recurrent state
motifs.description: Proposed learned resonant recurrence compared with ordinary attention and a nonoscillatory recurrent control; no outcome yet.
